content: The Bradley Method of natural childbirth, also referred to as husband-coached childbirth, was developed by Dr. Robert A. Bradley (1917–1998) and gained popularity through his book Husband-Coached Childbirth. This method is based on the belief that, with proper preparation, education, and the support of a loving and attentive coach, most women can successfully give birth naturally, without the need for drugs or surgical interventions. The Bradley Method emphasizes maintaining health and minimizing risks during pregnancy to avoid complications that might necessitate medical interventions. Its primary objective is to ensure the well-being of both the mother and the baby. The method advocates that, in most cases, natural childbirth—free from the use of drugs—is the optimal way to achieve this goal. Statistics show that over 86% of women who follow the Bradley Method and have vaginal births do so without the use of drugs. Classes in the Bradley Method focus on teaching nutrition, relaxation techniques, and natural breathing as tools for pain management. Additionally, the method encourages the active involvement of the husband or partner as a labor coach. Expectant parents are also educated on how to be informed consumers of childbirth services, empowering them to make well-informed decisions about procedures, birth attendants, and the choice of birth location. Dr. Bradley developed this method during a time when hospital deliveries often involved twilight sleep and general anesthesia, a practice he referred to as knock-em-out, drag-em-out obstetrics. Having grown up on a farm and observed numerous animal births, Dr. Bradley believed that human women, like the animals he had seen, could give birth without the need for drugs. He based his method on observations of laboring mammals, noting their instinctive behaviors during labor and delivery. He then adapted these principles to teach human women how to replicate these natural processes. When Dr. Bradley began trialing his method with pregnant nurses, he quickly recognized the importance of the father's presence and support during labor and delivery. He concluded that the involvement of the father significantly contributed to the mother's success in achieving a natural birth. As a result, Dr. Bradley became a pioneer in integrating fathers into the childbirth process. He expanded his method to include comprehensive training for fathers, preparing them to serve as effective labor coaches. Instructors of the Bradley Method are certified by the American Academy of Husband-Coached Childbirth (AAHCC). The terms Husband-Coached Childbirth® and The Bradley Method® are registered trademarks, ensuring that only individuals certified by the AAHCC are authorized to teach this method, thereby protecting consumers and maintaining the integrity of the program.
